title: Open Tree of Life web services
note: Topology and taxonomy context; divergence dates require separate evidence.

title: First Mesozoic mammal from Australia—an Early Cretaceous monotreme
authors: Archer, M.; Flannery, T.F.; Ritchie, A.; Molnar, R.E.
note: Primary description of AM F66763; monotreme affinity and tooth homologies are interpretations of the preserved dentary.

title: Genome analysis of the platypus reveals unique signatures of evolution
note: Primary genome assembly and comparative analysis of the female platypus Glennie; assembly and annotation limitations remain explicit.

title: The earliest known eutherian mammal
authors: Ji, Q.; Luo, Z.-X.; Yuan, C.-X.; Wible, J.R.; Zhang, J.-P.; Georgi, J.A.
note: Primary description of CAGS 01-IG-1a,b; later matrices have tested alternative placements, so the original eutherian position is not treated as immutable.

title: A Jurassic eutherian mammal and divergence of marsupials and placentals
authors: Luo, Z.-X.; Yuan, C.-X.; Meng, Q.-J.; Ji, Q.
note: Primary description and original Tiaojishan provenance and topology for BMNH PM1343B; those assignments are not converted into a universal calibration.

title: Tip dating supports novel resolutions of controversial relationships among early mammals
publisher: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
note: Primary Bayesian tip-dating sensitivity analysis; its unconstrained age estimate is a model output, not a redating of the rock specimen.

title: An Early Cretaceous eutherian and the placental–marsupial dichotomy
authors: Bi, S.; Zheng, X.; Wang, X.; Cignetti, N.E.; Yang, S.; Wible, J.R.
note: Primary description of STM33-5 and a morphology-matrix reassessment of Sinodelphys; the resulting topology remains dataset-dependent.

title: The placental mammal ancestor and the post–K–Pg radiation of placentals
note: Primary combined-data analysis using MorphoBank phenomic characters and GenBank sequences; reconstructed anatomy and node ages are model outputs.

title: Resolution of the early placental mammal radiation using Bayesian phylogenetics
note: Primary 16,397-base-pair Bayesian and maximum-likelihood analysis; topology, dating and biogeographic explanation are model-conditioned.

title: Paleocene emergence of elephant relatives and the rapid radiation of African ungulates
publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
note: Open primary description of the Eritherium hypodigm from Sidi Chennane; stem-proboscidean placement is matrix-based.

title: Gradual adaptation of bone structure to aquatic lifestyle in extinct sloths from Peru
authors: Amson, E.; de Muizon, C.; Laurin, M.; Argot, C.; de Buffrénil, V.
publisher: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
note: Open primary comparative histology and CT study; aquatic function is inferred from bone structure and stratigraphic succession, not directly observed behaviour.

title: A large mimotonid from the Middle Eocene of China sheds light on the evolution of lagomorphs and their kin
authors: Fostowicz-Frelik, Ł.; Li, C.; Mao, F.; Meng, J.; Wang, Y.
note: Open primary description of IVPP V20115 and referred teeth and tarsals; body mass and niche are comparative model inferences.

title: Primitive Early Eocene bat from Wyoming and the evolution of flight and echolocation
authors: Simmons, N.B.; Seymour, K.L.; Habersetzer, J.; Gunnell, G.F.
note: Primary description of ROM 55351A; flight and echolocation capability are functional inferences from preserved anatomy.

title: Molecular evidence regarding the origin of echolocation and flight in bats
authors: Teeling, E.C.; Scally, M.; Kao, D.J.; Romagnoli, M.L.; Springer, M.S.; Stanhope, M.J.
note: Primary seven-gene phylogenetic analysis; alternative gains or losses of laryngeal echolocation are historical inferences, not directly observed origins.

title: Cranial Anatomy of the Earliest Marsupials and the Origin of Opossums
authors: Horovitz, I.; Martin, T.; Bloch, J.; Ladevèze, S.; Kurz, C.; Sánchez-Villagra, M.R.
note: Primary cranial study and phylogenetic analysis of Peradectes and close metatherian relatives; the approximately 65.18 Ma calibration depends on the recovered crown placement.
